transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Lee. Well, what brings me in is that I just cannot keep my mind on one thing anymore. It's getting really frustrating. I'll be working, and just hearing one saw start up, or seeing somebody walk past the office, or even just having a passing thought about a different job... it completely pulls me off whatever I'm doing. And then, before I know it, the whole day just gets away from me.
Can you tell me when this difficulty staying focused first started — has it been a lifelong pattern since childhood, or is this something new that began more recently?

It's definitely a lifelong pattern. Even back in grade school, well before I was 12, my teachers were always telling my mother that I was bright but careless. I was always losing my homework, or forgetting instructions... just staring out the window instead of finishing my seatwork. So, yeah, it's been going on since I was a kid.
Besides the trouble focusing, do you also notice things like feeling restless, fidgeting, talking excessively, or acting impulsively without thinking things through?

I don't really notice the talking excessively or acting impulsively. But the restless part... yeah, I definitely get that. 

If I have to sit at the desk doing estimates for a job, or if I'm stuck sitting through a long meeting, I just feel really wound up inside. It's like I just need to get up and move around. Even though my wrist is healed up now and I know I’m supposed to just stay put and finish what I'm working on, it's really hard for me to just sit still.
Do you often find yourself interrupting conversations or blurting out responses before the other person has finished speaking?

No, not really. I don't think I do that. Like I mentioned a minute ago, the impulsive stuff or talking too much isn't really my problem. I might zone out and completely lose track of what the other person is saying, but I don't interrupt them or blurt things out.
Aside from work, do these same problems with focus and restlessness also cause noticeable difficulties in other areas of your life, like at home or in your relationships?

Yeah, it definitely spills over. At work, it's gotten pretty bad... my mistakes and delays have actually cost me commissions. I've had to redo work on jobs, and honestly, the rest of the crew is getting less willing to rely on me for things like scheduling or ordering materials. 

And at home... well, it's a problem there, too. My husband has pretty much had to take over paying the bills and keeping track of reminders. I just kept misplacing important papers or completely missing what needed to be done. So, yeah, it affects pretty much everything.
Have you been experiencing any persistent low mood, anxiety, or excessive worry recently that might be affecting your concentration?

No, not really. I mean, I get frustrated with myself for messing up at work and losing track of things at home, but I wouldn't say I'm depressed or constantly worrying about things. It's just the focus and the restlessness that are the real issues for me.
Do you drink alcohol, use recreational drugs, or have trouble sleeping that might be affecting your concentration?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I might have a beer or two on the weekend, but I don't really drink much, and I don't use any drugs. As for sleep... I sleep fine, honestly. I usually get a full night's rest. It's just during the day when I'm awake that I can't seem to keep my head straight. So, no, I don't think it's from any of that.

Since childhood, have these attention and restlessness difficulties been continuously present, or was there ever a stretch of months or years as a teen or adult when they got much better or went away?

No, they've never really gone away. It's just... always been like this. Even back in grade school, well before I was 12, my teachers were always telling my mother the same kind of things. They'd say I was bright, but careless. I was always losing my homework or forgetting instructions... just staring out the window instead of finishing my seatwork. So, yeah, it hasn't ever really stopped. It's been a continuous thing my whole life.

Symptoms cause significant functional impairment at work (lost commissions, redone jobs, decreased reliance from coworkers) and at home (spouse managing bills/reminders). Impulsivity and interrupting behaviors are denied, but the combination of prominent inattentive and hyperactive-restless symptoms without impulsivity still fits the ICD-10 category of Disturbance of Activity and Attention (F90.0), which encompasses combined inattentive/hyperactive presentations. Mood, anxiety, sleep, and substance use were explicitly ruled out as alternative explanations, and no significant depressive or anxious symptoms were endorsed.
